sources.name: Open-Meteo Climate API
sources.purpose: Daily max temperature and rainfall, 1950–2050, from 7 high-resolution climate models. Gives days ≥40 °C and the wettest day of the year, today and 2040.

outputs.role: Raw responses, one gzip per plant
Exact request URL, time, cost, checksum per plant
Heat days and wettest day per plant

caveats: Free tier: 10,000 weighted calls a day per IP; one plant (101 years × 14 columns) costs about 3,700, so a full refresh takes two days.
One high-emissions pathway (HighResMIP), so no scenario choice.
Not bias-corrected: heat-day counts look high. EC_Earth3P_HR has no 2050; NICAM16_8S has implausible temperatures. See Issues & notes.

sources.name: WRI Aqueduct 4.0
sources.purpose: Water stress today and in 2030/2050 under three scenarios, riverine and coastal flood risk scores (0–5) for each plant's river basin.
sources.request: Lookup per plant point in the Water Risk Atlas (see raw/aqueduct40_README.md). For a full rebuild: download the Aqueduct 4.0 baseline and future annual tables and basin geometry, then join each plant point to its basin.

outputs.role: Files as supplied (baseline, future, summary, README)

caveats: Lookups use approximate town-centre points; Satna's is 1.7 km from the register location.
2040 is the midpoint of 2030 and 2050 (estimated). Business-as-usual = SSP3-7.0.
Basin geometry and data dictionary are not in the repo; the lookup was done upstream.
Mundra's baseline row is malformed (two extra values); its drought and overall-risk fields are left empty.
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0, attribute World Resources Institute

sources.name: Open-Meteo Flood API
sources.purpose: Daily river discharge from 1984 (GloFAS). Planned as flood history for river plants (Chandrapur on the Wardha, Durgapur on the Damodar). Not used in the ₹ figures.
caveats: Grid cell is about 5 km; small rivers may not be resolved. Shares the Open-Meteo daily call limit.
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0, attribute Open-Meteo.com and GloFAS

sources.name: Nimbus Cement plant register
sources.purpose: The nine plants: location, type, capacity, output, clinker flows, water source, coastal flag, asset value, revenue.
sources.request: Supplied with the brief. Replace with the company's asset register for a real build.

outputs.role: Read by the API as is
Clinker flows (shipped tonnes and destinations from the register)

caveats: Clinker destinations come from the free-text notes column; check them against logistics data.

sources.name: India boundary (OpenStreetMap)
sources.purpose: National outline for the map, including India's full claimed boundary in Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh and Arunachal Pradesh.
sources.request: OSM relation for India, admin_level 2, exported as GeoJSON (supplied file).

outputs.role: Simplified outline served to the browser

caveats: National outline only; state shading would need a state-boundary file.

sources.name: CCTS emission-intensity targets (Government of India)
sources.purpose: Greenhouse Gases Emission Intensity Target Rules, 2025 under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme. Sets per-plant targets for cement (2025-26 and 2026-27 against a 2023-24 baseline).
sources.request: Download the gazette PDF; copy the cement schedule (entity, baseline and target intensity) into a CSV by hand.
caveats: Nimbus has no row in this list; a real build needs the company's own obligated-entity entry.
Final targets were reduced pro rata for the late notification; use the gazette, not the draft.

sources.name: ICAP factsheet: Indian Carbon Credit Trading Scheme
sources.purpose: Plain-language summary of the scheme's design: coverage, allocation, offsets and timeline.
sources.request: Read the factsheet; no data to load.
caveats: A secondary summary; cite the gazette for numbers.

sources.name: NGFS climate scenarios (IIASA Scenario Explorer)
sources.purpose: Carbon price paths to 2050 under orderly, disorderly and hot-house scenarios, to turn CCTS shortfalls into a ₹ cost.
sources.request: Log in as guest, open Downloads, take the IAMC-format CSV; filter region = India (or Asia), variable Price|Carbon.
caveats: Licence restricts redistributing substantial parts of the data; commit only the filtered rows.
Model-based shadow prices, not market prices.
NGFS warns that the paper behind its Phase V physical-damage estimates (Kotz et al., 2024) has been retracted. Use the transition variables (carbon prices), not the physical-damage outputs.
ngfs.net and the World Bank dashboard refuse scripted requests (HTTP 403); open them in a browser.

sources.name: World Bank Carbon Pricing Dashboard
sources.purpose: Which carbon taxes and trading schemes exist, their coverage and prices, for comparing India with peers.
sources.request: Download the data file from the dashboard (Excel).
caveats: Annual snapshot; India's scheme has no traded price yet.

sources.name: ICAP Allowance Price Explorer
sources.purpose: Historical allowance prices for existing trading schemes, as reference points for a future Indian credit price.
sources.request: Select the schemes and download the price series.
caveats: Prices are in local currency; convert with a stated exchange rate.
